Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

The Present Simple — your routine, every day.
Track 2.3 — six verbsOriginal coursebook recording
Track 2.4 — the three soundsOriginal coursebook recording
1goes — which sound?
2teaches — which sound?
3cooks — which sound?
4relaxes — which sound?
5makes — which sound?
6plays — which sound?
Why

/s/ after quiet sounds (cooks, makes) · /z/ after noisy sounds (goes, plays) · /ɪz/ after -ch, -x, -sh, -s (teaches, relaxes).

1plays — which sound?
2relaxes — which sound?
3makes — which sound?
4teaches — which sound?
Why

/s/ after quiet sounds (makes) · /z/ after noisy sounds (plays) · /ɪz/ after -ch, -x, -sh, -s (teaches, relaxes).

1plays — which sound?
2relaxes — which sound?
3makes — which sound?
4teaches — which sound?
Why

/s/ after quiet sounds (makes) · /z/ after noisy sounds (plays) · /ɪz/ after -ch, -x, -sh, -s (teaches, relaxes).

In other words
“I get up at six.”
“We watch the sunrise together.”
“She takes the bus to work.”
“He goes to bed at eight.”
Notice

Notice: look at the verbs after she and he. What is different?

PersonExample
I / you / we / theyI get up early. · They take the bus.
he / she / itHe gets up early. · She takes the bus.
spellinggo → goes · watch → watches · study → studies · have → has
In other words
Use the Present Simple for routines — things you do every day, every week.
After he / she / it the verb takes -s: he works, she gets up.
Spelling: watch → watches, go → goes, study → studies. have → has is irregular.
The -s is only for he/she/it: “I gets up” ✗ → “I get up” ✓.
How to say NO (don't / doesn't) comes in Lesson 8.

Stage 9 · Listen

Listen

Track 2.1 — a day in the life of a scientistOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
I'm a scientist. I study penguins on Bird Island and I'm very happy here. In the summer, my days are long. I get up early and go to the beach. I watch the penguins with their babies. I sometimes go out in a boat with the other scientists on the island. We visit different islands and take photos of the birds and animals there. I often work all day and I only stop in the evening to have dinner. I sometimes go back to the beach after dinner to spend more time with the penguins. Then I work in the lab. I always go to bed late! In the winter, the weather is always very cold, but we usually have more free time and I can relax.
A scientist lives on Bird Island and watches penguins.

Listen once. Then choose True or False.

1He gets up early and goes to the beach.
2He only works in the mornings.
3He sometimes goes back to the beach after dinner.
4In winter he never has free time.
Why

He often works all day and only stops in the evening. In winter they usually have more free time.

A scientist lives on Bird Island and watches penguins.

Listen once. Then answer the questions.

1What does he watch?
2When does he stop work?
3In winter he usually has ___ free time.
Why

He watches penguins, often works all day and stops in the evening. In winter they usually have more free time.

Show transcript
1 — British people never have fish for breakfast. They usually have toast or cereal. 2 — They are hardly ever late for meetings. They like to arrive on time. 3 — British people sometimes go to a different city to study at university. 4 — British people often have more than one TV at home: some people have three or four. 5 — They usually eat lunch at work. They don't have time to go home. 6 — And British people always, always talk about the weather!
First, listen to six facts about British habits.

Then write about your own perfect day.

1British people usually have ___ for breakfast.
2They are hardly ever ___ for meetings.
Why

They never have fish for breakfast — they usually have toast or cereal. And they are hardly ever late.

Useful language

  • I wake up at…

  • I hardly ever…

Make notes. Then report to another pair.

Interview your teacher about their perfect day.

Make notes. Then report to your teacher.

Useful language
  • What time do you wake up?
  • How often do you…?
  • I always / usually…
  • I hardly ever…
  • She wakes up at…
  • He never…
In other words
• What time do you get up on weekdays?
• What do you do first in the morning?
• How do you get to work or school?
• What do you usually have for lunch?
• How often do you cook dinner?
• What do you do in the evening?
• How often do you do sport?
• What do you do on Saturdays?
• What time do you usually go to bed?
• What does your best friend do every day? (careful: he gets, she goes!)
In other words
Step 1 — ask your partner: What time do you wake up on your perfect day? What do you do in the morning / afternoon / evening? How often do you…?
Step 2 — swap roles.
Step 3 — tell another pair about your partner's day. Use he / she + -s: “She wakes up at ten. She never does the housework!”
In other words
Step 1 — ask your teacher: What time do you wake up on your perfect day? What do you do in the morning / afternoon / evening? How often do you…?
Step 2 — swap roles.
Step 3 — tell your teacher about your teacher's day. Use he / she + -s: “She wakes up at ten. She never does the housework!”
Stage 11 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1She ___ up at seven. (get)
2He ___ to work by bus. (go)
3My father ___ TV in the evening. (watch)
Why

he/she/it + verb-s: gets, goes, watches, has \u00b7 negative: doesn't + base verb.

1She get up at seven.
2He watch TV in the evening.
3My brother go to work by bus.
Why

he/she/it + verb-s: gets, goes, watches, has \u00b7 negative: doesn't + base verb.

1Change to SHE: I get up early.
2Change to SHE: I have breakfast at eight.
3Make it negative: He works on Saturdays.
Why

he/she/it + verb-s: gets, goes, watches, has \u00b7 negative: doesn't + base verb.
